<reflection>
The previous experiment (doubling catalyst to 0.02 M) successfully spread the negative log-likelihood values, clearly separating a group of deactivation mechanisms (M20, M11, M15, etc., with NLL ~ -40) from others (NLL ~ -27). This indicates that the aim of discriminating among mechanisms was achieved, as the increased catalyst concentration stressed dimerization and deactivation pathways, making deactivation models fit better. However, multiple mechanisms remain plausible with similar NLLs, requiring further discrimination.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To further discriminate among the plausible mechanisms, I propose adding initial product to the reaction mixture. This will directly probe mechanisms involving product deactivation (M12, M17) and reversibility in all mechanisms. By comparing with run 1 (same substrate and catalyst but no product), the effect of product on the reaction rate and potential deactivation can be observed. This design is effective because it targets product-dependent steps across multiple mechanisms simultaneously, including M12 (deactivation by product on catalyst), M17 (deactivation by product on catalyst-substrate complex), and reversibility in others. It avoids extreme conditions and adds a new dimension (initial product) not yet explored, enhancing discrimination over the entire set.
</hypothesis>
